items.step: Add workspace plan selection defaults and ambiguity gates
acceptance: `ST_WORKSPACE` supplies the default workspace root when `--workspace` is omitted.
`ST_PLAN` supplies the default plan ID when `--plan` is omitted and the plan is registered and active.
A plan-local command with workspace mode and exactly one active registered plan infers that plan when no explicit plan is supplied.
A plan-local command with workspace mode and two or more active registered plans fails closed without mutating any plan.
CLI `--workspace` and `--plan` override environment defaults, and legacy `--file` behavior remains unchanged when no workspace mode is requested.

contract.objective: Implement the plan selection rules for workspace-scoped legacy commands without introducing session binding, claims, cross-plan dependencies, or worker semantics.
contract.background: Explicit workspace plan routing now works, but compatibility mode still requires callers to pass both `--workspace` and `--plan`. The specification requires environment defaults and safe inference so one-plan workspace operation remains ergonomic while multi-plan ambiguity fails closed.
contract.implementation_approach: Track whether workspace and plan scope came from CLI or environment, apply `ST_WORKSPACE` and `ST_PLAN` before command dispatch, then infer a plan only when workspace mode is active and the latest workspace registry has exactly one active plan. If more than one active plan exists and no explicit or environment plan was supplied, return a missing/ambiguous plan-scope error before any mutation.
success_criteria: `ST_WORKSPACE` supplies the default workspace root when `--workspace` is omitted.
`ST_PLAN` supplies the default plan ID when `--plan` is omitted and the plan is registered and active.
A plan-local command with workspace mode and exactly one active registered plan infers that plan when no explicit plan is supplied.
A plan-local command with workspace mode and two or more active registered plans fails closed without mutating any plan.
CLI `--workspace` and `--plan` override environment defaults, and legacy `--file` behavior remains unchanged when no workspace mode is requested.
risks: Environment defaults must not accidentally turn legacy `--file` commands into workspace commands.
Ambiguity checks must happen before plan-local mutations and must not create plan files.

items.step: Add workspace plan lifecycle commands
acceptance: `st plan pause --workspace PATH --plan PLAN_ID` changes an active plan registry record to paused and increments workspace sequence.
`st plan resume --workspace PATH --plan PLAN_ID` changes a paused plan registry record back to active and increments workspace sequence.
`st plan complete --workspace PATH --plan PLAN_ID` changes an active or paused plan registry record to completed and excludes it from active-plan inference.
`st plan archive --workspace PATH --plan PLAN_ID` changes a non-active plan registry record to archived and excludes it from active-plan inference.
Unknown plans and invalid lifecycle transitions fail closed without mutating `workspace.jsonl`.
Existing create/list/show behavior remains compatible.

contract.objective: Implement the plan lifecycle command subset without introducing sessions, claims, cross-plan dependencies, changesets, or integration semantics.
contract.background: The workspace registry can create and route active plans, and plan selection now infers only when exactly one active plan exists. The registry still has no state transitions, so active-plan inference cannot be controlled without deleting or bypassing plans.
contract.implementation_approach: Extend the `st plan` command group with pause/resume/complete/archive. Load the latest STW-v1 checkpoint, validate the target plan exists, validate the allowed state transition, append a new checkpoint with the updated plan record, and preserve all other workspace fields. Reuse the existing active-plan inference logic so paused/completed/archived plans do not count as active.
success_criteria: `st plan pause --workspace PATH --plan PLAN_ID` changes an active plan registry record to paused and increments workspace sequence.
`st plan resume --workspace PATH --plan PLAN_ID` changes a paused plan registry record back to active and increments workspace sequence.
`st plan complete --workspace PATH --plan PLAN_ID` changes an active or paused plan registry record to completed and excludes it from active-plan inference.
`st plan archive --workspace PATH --plan PLAN_ID` changes a non-active plan registry record to archived and excludes it from active-plan inference.
Unknown plans and invalid lifecycle transitions fail closed without mutating `workspace.jsonl`.
Existing create/list/show behavior remains compatible.
risks: Lifecycle transitions must not rewrite plan graph files or mutate unrelated plan records.
Archive should not hide still-active work silently; active plans must be paused or completed before archive.

items.step: Add qualified refs and cross-plan link commands
acceptance: `st plan link --workspace PATH --from plan://A/ITEM --to plan://B/ITEM --type hard` appends a workspace-owned cross-plan edge after validating both plans and local items.
`st plan link --type nonblocking` records a nonblocking edge without changing plan-local graph files.
`st plan unlink --workspace PATH --from plan://A/ITEM --to plan://B/ITEM [--type TYPE]` removes the matching workspace-owned edge.
Malformed qualified refs, unknown plans, unknown items, duplicate links, and missing links fail closed without mutating `workspace.jsonl`.
Workspace status/list/show preserve existing behavior, and plan-local graph files remain independent.

contract.objective: Implement the smallest cross-plan edge kernel: qualified reference parsing and workspace-owned link/unlink commands, without implementing readiness propagation, cycle detection, claims, sessions, resources, or integration.
contract.background: Plan namespace, routing, selection, and lifecycle are present, but cross-plan dependency authority is still absent. The spec requires workspace-owned qualified references so different plan IDs do not imply safe concurrency and cross-plan relationships are not hidden inside one plan graph.
contract.implementation_approach: Add `plan link` and `plan unlink` subcommands with `--from`, `--to`, and `--type hard|nonblocking`. Parse `plan://PLAN_ID/LOCAL_ID` through a helper, validate plan IDs through the registry, validate item IDs by loading each registered plan graph, and append or remove edge records under `cross_plan_edges` in a new STW-v1 checkpoint. Preserve all other workspace fields and all plan graph files unchanged.
success_criteria: `st plan link --workspace PATH --from plan://A/ITEM --to plan://B/ITEM --type hard` appends a workspace-owned cross-plan edge after validating both plans and local items.
`st plan link --type nonblocking` records a nonblocking edge without changing plan-local graph files.
`st plan unlink --workspace PATH --from plan://A/ITEM --to plan://B/ITEM [--type TYPE]` removes the matching workspace-owned edge.
Malformed qualified refs, unknown plans, unknown items, duplicate links, and missing links fail closed without mutating `workspace.jsonl`.
Workspace status/list/show preserve existing behavior, and plan-local graph files remain independent.
risks: Edge orientation must be explicit and stable: `from` is the dependent item and `to` is the referenced item.
Link validation must not create missing plan files or silently accept unknown local IDs.

items.step: Harden durable-store transactions for workspace files
acceptance: Mutating workspace paths use a short lock, expected sequence check, prepare journal, atomic publish, and commit record.
Recovery detects incomplete prepared transactions and either completes or reports `workspace_recovery_required` without silent mutation.
Direct workspace append/write helpers are no longer used for workspace authority updates.
Transaction and lock files reject symlink replacement and stay under `.ledger/st/transactions` and `.ledger/st/locks`.

contract.objective: Provide the durable-store kernel needed by later concurrency work: sequence CAS, journaled publish, and explicit recovery for workspace JSONL.
contract.background: Workspace init, registry, lifecycle, and link commands exist, but they still rely on localized file writes. The spec requires every mutation to pass through a durable transaction boundary.
contract.implementation_approach: Extend `libs/durable_store` with a small transaction API and switch workspace writers in `apps/st/scripts/st.zig` to consume it. Keep legacy `.step/st-plan.jsonl` graph mutation behavior unchanged unless it is explicitly part of workspace mode.
success_criteria: Mutating workspace paths use a short lock, expected sequence check, prepare journal, atomic publish, and commit record.
Recovery detects incomplete prepared transactions and either completes or reports `workspace_recovery_required` without silent mutation.
Direct workspace append/write helpers are no longer used for workspace authority updates.
Transaction and lock files reject symlink replacement and stay under `.ledger/st/transactions` and `.ledger/st/locks`.
risks: Recovery must not treat partially written checkpoints as authoritative.
Lock scope must stay short and cannot cover build, test, or proof execution.

items.step: Implement resource grammar normalization and conflict detection
acceptance: `path:`, `symbol:`, `generated:`, `schema:`, `service:`, `git:index`, `git:branch:BRANCH`, and `repo:all` resources parse into normalized records.
Absolute paths, `..`, NUL bytes, malformed names, and symlink escapes are rejected.
Path ancestor and descendant overlap conflicts, and symbol resources inherit file-level conflicts.
Read/read is compatible, read/write and write/write conflict, and exclusive conflicts with every mode.
Unknown or low-confidence mutation scope maps to `repo:all` exclusive authority.

contract.objective: Add the conservative resource kernel used by claims, workspace aperture, change-set sealing, and integration.
contract.background: Workspace links exist but concurrency cannot be safe without one shared resource grammar and conflict model.
contract.implementation_approach: Introduce resource parsing and conflict helpers inside the current `st` surface first, with tests covering malformed resources, path overlap, symbol inheritance, Git resources, and mode matrix behavior.
success_criteria: `path:`, `symbol:`, `generated:`, `schema:`, `service:`, `git:index`, `git:branch:BRANCH`, and `repo:all` resources parse into normalized records.
Absolute paths, `..`, NUL bytes, malformed names, and symlink escapes are rejected.
Path ancestor and descendant overlap conflicts, and symbol resources inherit file-level conflicts.
Read/read is compatible, read/write and write/write conflict, and exclusive conflicts with every mode.
Unknown or low-confidence mutation scope maps to `repo:all` exclusive authority.
risks: Path normalization must be repository-root relative and cannot trust caller-supplied paths.
Compatibility inference must fail closed rather than grant optimistic concurrency.

items.step: Add workspace-global claims, leases, and fencing tokens
acceptance: `st claim` grants workspace-global claims with resource sets, lease expiry, and monotonic fencing tokens.
`st claim heartbeat`, `show`, `list`, `release`, `reclaim-stale`, `conflicts`, and `amend` enforce owner, session, token, and expected sequence checks.
Conflicting held claims are denied with `resource_conflict`; stale expected sequence and stale fencing fail with distinct errors.
Reclaim marks an old claim stale and never revalidates the old fencing token.
Amend behaves as release-and-regrant and always allocates a new token.

contract.objective: Move claim authority to workspace state while preserving legacy compatibility where workspace mode is not active.
contract.background: The legacy graph claim command is plan-local. STW-v1 requires workspace-global authority because different plan IDs do not imply safe concurrency.
contract.implementation_approach: Layer workspace claim records over the resource conflict kernel, allocate fencing tokens through workspace sequence transactions, and keep old heartbeat as a compatibility alias for claim heartbeat.
success_criteria: `st claim` grants workspace-global claims with resource sets, lease expiry, and monotonic fencing tokens.
`st claim heartbeat`, `show`, `list`, `release`, `reclaim-stale`, `conflicts`, and `amend` enforce owner, session, token, and expected sequence checks.
Conflicting held claims are denied with `resource_conflict`; stale expected sequence and stale fencing fail with distinct errors.
Reclaim marks an old claim stale and never revalidates the old fencing token.
Amend behaves as release-and-regrant and always allocates a new token.
risks: Old tokens must remain invalid forever after release or reclaim.
Compatibility aliases must not bypass workspace fencing.

items.step: Add session binding and independent session views
acceptance: `st session bind`, `show`, `switch-plan`, `release`, and `list` create and validate SVW-v1 runtime records.
Session views include executor, plan, claim, fencing token, workspace sequence, plan sequence, branch epoch, selected IDs, target, and projection digest.
`prime`, `assert-projection`, and `reconcile-codex` operate on the caller session without overwriting other sessions.
Session A cannot reconcile or assert Session B's projection.
Switching plans requires release of incompatible held authority.

contract.objective: Introduce SVW-v1 session views and route projection commands through session state in workspace mode.
contract.background: The current projection model is durable and shared. STW-v1 requires projection state to be session-scoped so two agents can work concurrently when claims prove compatibility.
contract.implementation_approach: Store runtime session and view files under `.ledger/st/runtime`, digest the compiled projection, and keep plan-local selected flags only as migrated compatibility input.
success_criteria: `st session bind`, `show`, `switch-plan`, `release`, and `list` create and validate SVW-v1 runtime records.
Session views include executor, plan, claim, fencing token, workspace sequence, plan sequence, branch epoch, selected IDs, target, and projection digest.
`prime`, `assert-projection`, and `reconcile-codex` operate on the caller session without overwriting other sessions.
Session A cannot reconcile or assert Session B's projection.
Switching plans requires release of incompatible held authority.
risks: Session defaults must not leak across sessions through environment variables.
Projection drift must fail closed rather than silently reconciling stale rows.

items.step: Implement workspace aperture and cross-plan readiness gating
acceptance: `st workspace aperture` emits WAP-v1 with workspace sequence, branch epoch, allocations, and rejected candidates.
Hard cross-plan dependencies block readiness until the qualified target is complete.
Nonblocking cross-plan links do not gate execution.
Deterministic greedy selection uses score, fairness debt, and qualified ID ordering.
Candidate conflicts report the conflicting held claim or candidate.

contract.objective: Add the first workspace aperture kernel that chooses safe candidate work across active plans without mutating plan state until claim grant.
contract.background: Plan-local aperture exists and cross-plan links can be recorded, but there is no global workspace selection authority.
contract.implementation_approach: Compile ready candidates per active plan, apply hard cross-plan dependency gates, build a conflict graph from candidate resources and held claims, and emit deterministic WAP-v1 receipts.
success_criteria: `st workspace aperture` emits WAP-v1 with workspace sequence, branch epoch, allocations, and rejected candidates.
Hard cross-plan dependencies block readiness until the qualified target is complete.
Nonblocking cross-plan links do not gate execution.
Deterministic greedy selection uses score, fairness debt, and qualified ID ordering.
Candidate conflicts report the conflicting held claim or candidate.
risks: A selected candidate set is advisory only; mutation authority still belongs to claim grant.
Cycle detection can remain conservative but must fail closed when discovered.

items.step: Emit GCR-v2 execution authority receipts
acceptance: GCR-v2 generation validates graph audit, workspace claim state, resources, session view digest, branch state, debt, waivers, and fencing token.
Receipts include workspace sequence, plan sequence, branch epoch, claim ID, fencing token, resource set, and execution_allowed.
Any stale workspace sequence, plan sequence, graph fingerprint, branch epoch, claim state, fencing token, or view digest denies execution.
Callers cannot override `execution_allowed`.

contract.objective: Upgrade execution permission receipts to GCR-v2 without deleting legacy GCR-v1 compatibility.
contract.background: Current GCR support proves only plan-local authority. STW-v1 requires workspace authority before workers mutate.
contract.implementation_approach: Add a workspace-mode GCR path that consumes current workspace, plan, claim, session, and branch-state records and emits machine-readable receipts for `$seq`.
success_criteria: GCR-v2 generation validates graph audit, workspace claim state, resources, session view digest, branch state, debt, waivers, and fencing token.
Receipts include workspace sequence, plan sequence, branch epoch, claim ID, fencing token, resource set, and execution_allowed.
Any stale workspace sequence, plan sequence, graph fingerprint, branch epoch, claim state, fencing token, or view digest denies execution.
Callers cannot override `execution_allowed`.
risks: Stale proof should be diagnosed precisely enough for controllers to recover.
Debt and waiver state must be part of currentness, not advisory text.

items.step: Add external worktrees and claim-bound change sets
acceptance: `st worktree create` creates a detached external worktree at target head and records metadata under `.ledger/st/worktrees`.
Nested primary-checkout worktrees and wrong Git common directories are rejected.
`st changeset seal`, `show`, `reject`, and `supersede` validate claim and fencing, derive changed paths from Git, reject outside-claim paths, compute patch and tree digests, and write CS-v1.
Supersession cannot mutate integrated or rejected change sets.
Dirty abandoned worktrees become recovery items instead of being silently deleted.

contract.objective: Bind worktree creation and worker output to claims so changed files cannot escape resource authority.
contract.background: Claims and GCR receipts authorize execution, but worker outputs need a sealed boundary before integration.
contract.implementation_approach: Use Git to create external worktrees and derive diffs, store worktree metadata and change-set receipts under `.ledger/st`, and refuse caller-supplied changed paths.
success_criteria: `st worktree create` creates a detached external worktree at target head and records metadata under `.ledger/st/worktrees`.
Nested primary-checkout worktrees and wrong Git common directories are rejected.
`st changeset seal`, `show`, `reject`, and `supersede` validate claim and fencing, derive changed paths from Git, reject outside-claim paths, compute patch and tree digests, and write CS-v1.
Supersession cannot mutate integrated or rejected change sets.
Dirty abandoned worktrees become recovery items instead of being silently deleted.
risks: Machine-specific worktree paths must remain local runtime metadata.
Dirty recovery must preserve evidence without publishing local machine state.

items.step: Implement serialized target-branch integration
acceptance: `st integrate enqueue`, `status`, `preview`, `apply`, `reject`, and `recover` manage an ordered integration queue.
Integration obtains global Git resources and validates expected target head and branch epoch before apply.
Apply uses an alternate index or clean integration worktree and excludes unrelated primary-checkout dirt.
Textual or semantic conflicts leave the target branch unchanged and emit conflict artifacts.
Successful integration runs declared proof, advances the branch by compare-and-swap, increments branch epoch, and emits IGR-v1.

contract.objective: Add the controller-owned integration lane that safely advances one target branch from queued change sets.
contract.background: Workers may produce sealed change sets concurrently, but target branch mutation must be serialized and compare-and-swap bound.
contract.implementation_approach: Represent queue entries and receipts under `.ledger/st/integration`, guard Git resources with workspace claims, and perform apply/proof/commit through an isolated index or worktree.
success_criteria: `st integrate enqueue`, `status`, `preview`, `apply`, `reject`, and `recover` manage an ordered integration queue.
Integration obtains global Git resources and validates expected target head and branch epoch before apply.
Apply uses an alternate index or clean integration worktree and excludes unrelated primary-checkout dirt.
Textual or semantic conflicts leave the target branch unchanged and emit conflict artifacts.
Successful integration runs declared proof, advances the branch by compare-and-swap, increments branch epoch, and emits IGR-v1.
risks: Integration proof failure must leave the branch unchanged.
Worker agents must not gain a direct target-push path.

items.step: Bind proof receipts to branch epochs and dependency cuts
acceptance: PRF-v3 receipts include workspace ID, workspace sequence, plan ID, plan sequence, branch epoch, tree digest, dependency resources, item ID, and obligation ID.
Integration computes changed resources and stales final proof on every epoch change.
Focused and wave proof invalidation intersects change sets with dependency cuts and leaves disjoint focused proof current.
Historical proof receipts are retained.
Expired-claim proof requires revalidation before completion.

contract.objective: Prevent stale proof from surviving target branch changes while preserving historical evidence.
contract.background: Proof receipts exist, but they are not yet bound to workspace branch epochs and affected dependency cuts.
contract.implementation_approach: Add a proof index keyed by branch epoch, tree digest, resources, plan, item, and obligation, and update readiness after integrations invalidate affected cuts.
success_criteria: PRF-v3 receipts include workspace ID, workspace sequence, plan ID, plan sequence, branch epoch, tree digest, dependency resources, item ID, and obligation ID.
Integration computes changed resources and stales final proof on every epoch change.
Focused and wave proof invalidation intersects change sets with dependency cuts and leaves disjoint focused proof current.
Historical proof receipts are retained.
Expired-claim proof requires revalidation before completion.
risks: Broad invalidation is safe but may be expensive; narrow invalidation must not miss affected proof.
Historical receipt retention must not imply current execution authority.

items.step: Implement atomic migration from legacy `.step` plans
acceptance: `st workspace migrate --from .step/st-plan.jsonl --to .ledger/st --plan-id default` creates a workspace and plan graph only after parity audit passes.
Migration preserves IDs, statuses, dependencies, graph envelope, intent, waivers, debt, proof actions, receipts, polish, fingerprints, sequence, events, checkpoints, and source metadata.
Parity failure leaves the legacy file authoritative and does not publish partial workspace state.
Successful migration writes a receipt and optionally archives source bytes under `.ledger/st/migration/source`.
Workspace mode denies legacy writes and rejects mixed `--file` plus `--workspace` mutation.

contract.objective: Provide atomic migration and compatibility gates so existing one-plan users can move without losing graph-mode features.
contract.background: The repository still carries a single canonical `.step/st-plan.jsonl`. STW-v1 requires `.ledger/st` as the only writable canonical root after migration.
contract.implementation_approach: Read the legacy graph through existing validated loaders, emit workspace and plan checkpoints through durable transactions, run parity comparison before publish, and make post-migration legacy writes fail closed.
success_criteria: `st workspace migrate --from .step/st-plan.jsonl --to .ledger/st --plan-id default` creates a workspace and plan graph only after parity audit passes.
Migration preserves IDs, statuses, dependencies, graph envelope, intent, waivers, debt, proof actions, receipts, polish, fingerprints, sequence, events, checkpoints, and source metadata.
Parity failure leaves the legacy file authoritative and does not publish partial workspace state.
Successful migration writes a receipt and optionally archives source bytes under `.ledger/st/migration/source`.
Workspace mode denies legacy writes and rejects mixed `--file` plus `--workspace` mutation.
risks: Migration must be idempotent.
Compatibility reads must not reopen `.step` as a writable root.

items.step: Complete workspace audit, import/export, capabilities, and docs
acceptance: `st capabilities --format json` truthfully reports implemented STW-v1, graph schema, transaction, claim, session, resource, GCR, changeset, integration, proof, and migration capabilities.
`st workspace audit`, `doctor`, `recover`, `export`, and `import` produce machine-readable receipts and fail closed on ambiguity.
README documents workspace storage, plan selection rules, qualified refs, claims, sessions, change sets, integration, migration, and compatibility mode.
End-to-end smoke covers two plans, two sessions, disjoint claims, serialized integration, branch epoch increment, proof invalidation, and complete lineage reconstruction.
Release metadata reflects the implemented `st` version.

contract.objective: Close the STW-v1 release surface with accurate capabilities, recovery/audit commands, docs, and end-to-end validation.
contract.background: After the main workspace authority paths exist, the command surface and receipts must be coherent enough for users, controllers, and `$seq`.
contract.implementation_approach: Wire final command aliases and receipt schemas, refresh capability booleans only for implemented behavior, add end-to-end tests, update docs and version metadata, and run aggregate validation.
success_criteria: `st capabilities --format json` truthfully reports implemented STW-v1, graph schema, transaction, claim, session, resource, GCR, changeset, integration, proof, and migration capabilities.
`st workspace audit`, `doctor`, `recover`, `export`, and `import` produce machine-readable receipts and fail closed on ambiguity.
README documents workspace storage, plan selection rules, qualified refs, claims, sessions, change sets, integration, migration, and compatibility mode.
End-to-end smoke covers two plans, two sessions, disjoint claims, serialized integration, branch epoch increment, proof invalidation, and complete lineage reconstruction.
Release metadata reflects the implemented `st` version.
risks: Capability flags must not overclaim future work.
End-to-end tests need to avoid depending on machine-specific Git state.

items.step: Define durable-store concurrency API surface
acceptance: Public types include `Owner`, `AcquireOptions`, `LeaseLock`, `ReclaimReceipt`, `CasExpectation`, `CasWriteReceipt`, transaction records, recovery status/receipt, snapshot/commit receipts, and semantic errors named by the spec.
Existing public functions keep their current signatures and behavior.
New receipt renderers emit canonical JSON with stable schema/version fields.
Compile-time tests prove the public API compiles without requiring `apps/st`.

contract.objective: Introduce the stable public boundary and semantic error vocabulary for the new substrate before moving consumers.
contract.background: `durable_store` currently owns atomic replace, create-new, JSONL validation, basic locks, and a narrow JSONL checkpoint transaction. The new concurrency substrate must be reusable by `apps/st` and later `.ledger` controllers without silently changing legacy callers.
contract.implementation_approach: Add types and small canonical receipt helpers in `libs/durable_store/src/lib.zig`, keeping new APIs internally minimal until later items fill behavior. Do not remove or rename legacy APIs.
success_criteria: Public types include `Owner`, `AcquireOptions`, `LeaseLock`, `ReclaimReceipt`, `CasExpectation`, `CasWriteReceipt`, transaction records, recovery status/receipt, snapshot/commit receipts, and semantic errors named by the spec.
Existing public functions keep their current signatures and behavior.
New receipt renderers emit canonical JSON with stable schema/version fields.
Compile-time tests prove the public API compiles without requiring `apps/st`.
risks: Public API churn after consumers migrate would force broad rework.
New error names must stay semantic enough for `$st` exit-code mapping.

items.step: Implement lease locks and fencing counters
acceptance: `acquireLeaseLock`, `refreshLease`, `releaseLease`, and `reclaimExpiredLease` write and validate DLK-v1 metadata with owner, lease expiry, fencing token, and optional transaction id.
Acquisition supports timeout and retry without holding locks across caller work.
Fencing counters allocate atomically, never reuse tokens after reclaim, reject caller-provided tokens, fail on overflow, and mark corrupt counters recovery-required.
Reclaim requires expired lease, stale token relative to authority counter, and insufficient current owner authority; it emits evidence instead of silently deleting records.

contract.objective: Provide the short-lived lock and monotonic token authority used by CAS and transaction writers.
contract.background: Legacy locks are empty exclusive files. Multi-plan `$st` needs fencing authority so stale workers cannot act after lease reclamation.
contract.implementation_approach: Use exclusive create for lock acquisition, canonical JSON for metadata, no-follow/path checks before every lock operation, and a small authority counter file updated through the same secure create/rename discipline.
success_criteria: `acquireLeaseLock`, `refreshLease`, `releaseLease`, and `reclaimExpiredLease` write and validate DLK-v1 metadata with owner, lease expiry, fencing token, and optional transaction id.
Acquisition supports timeout and retry without holding locks across caller work.
Fencing counters allocate atomically, never reuse tokens after reclaim, reject caller-provided tokens, fail on overflow, and mark corrupt counters recovery-required.
Reclaim requires expired lease, stale token relative to authority counter, and insufficient current owner authority; it emits evidence instead of silently deleting records.
risks: Process liveness is not sufficient across namespaces and must not be the only reclaim proof.
Counter corruption must block authority rather than reset to a convenient value.

items.step: Implement CAS writes and JSONL snapshots
acceptance: `writeTextAtomicCas` checks expected digest, expected sequence, and expected existence immediately before publish and returns a receipt with before/after digest and sequence.
Digest, sequence, and existence mismatches return `DigestMismatch`, `SequenceMismatch`, `ExpectationMismatch`, or equivalent semantic errors.
`readJsonlSnapshot` validates JSONL and optional expected sequence while preserving file-size limits.
`commitJsonlSnapshotCas` validates the candidate snapshot and commits through CAS rather than read-append-rewrite.
Existing `writeTextAtomic`, `appendLineAtomic`, and validation tests still pass unchanged.

contract.objective: Prevent lost updates for single-file text and JSONL state while preserving legacy atomic replace behavior.
contract.background: The current transaction helper checks sequence inside a single lock path, but the reusable substrate needs explicit CAS receipts and snapshot APIs.
contract.implementation_approach: Compute canonical digests from bytes, derive sequence through JSONL field extraction where requested, validate all expectations after secure open and before rename, then publish with fsync and rename.
success_criteria: `writeTextAtomicCas` checks expected digest, expected sequence, and expected existence immediately before publish and returns a receipt with before/after digest and sequence.
Digest, sequence, and existence mismatches return `DigestMismatch`, `SequenceMismatch`, `ExpectationMismatch`, or equivalent semantic errors.
`readJsonlSnapshot` validates JSONL and optional expected sequence while preserving file-size limits.
`commitJsonlSnapshotCas` validates the candidate snapshot and commits through CAS rather than read-append-rewrite.
Existing `writeTextAtomic`, `appendLineAtomic`, and validation tests still pass unchanged.
risks: Sequence extraction must reject malformed JSONL rather than infer a default for existing corrupt files.
CAS receipts must not expose secrets from file contents.

items.step: Implement durable transactions and recovery
acceptance: DTX-v1 transactions normalize and sort resources, acquire locks in canonical order, validate all expectations, stage writes, fsync staged files and transaction records, mark prepared, publish deterministically, write commit marker, fsync containing directories where supported, release locks, and retain bounded receipts.
`inspectTransaction` and `recoverTransaction` distinguish finish-commit, rollback-unpublished, committed, aborted, corrupt, and manual-recovery-required states.
Recovery never guesses when published files disagree with expected transaction digests.
Duplicate canonical-path aliases and unsafe transaction paths are rejected.

contract.objective: Make transaction recovery deterministic for workspace plus plan mutation and reusable by future `.ledger` controllers.
contract.background: `apps/st` has workspace transactions but the durable substrate does not yet own multi-file prepare/commit/recovery.
contract.implementation_approach: Model transaction directories as evidence stores, keep staged bytes immutable after prepare, publish with deterministic order, and make recovery decide only from durable markers plus digest checks.
success_criteria: DTX-v1 transactions normalize and sort resources, acquire locks in canonical order, validate all expectations, stage writes, fsync staged files and transaction records, mark prepared, publish deterministically, write commit marker, fsync containing directories where supported, release locks, and retain bounded receipts.
`inspectTransaction` and `recoverTransaction` distinguish finish-commit, rollback-unpublished, committed, aborted, corrupt, and manual-recovery-required states.
Recovery never guesses when published files disagree with expected transaction digests.
Duplicate canonical-path aliases and unsafe transaction paths are rejected.
risks: Cross-platform fsync support differs; unsupported directory fsync must be reported without weakening the commit protocol.
Partial publishes must not be presented as valid logical state.

items.step: Migrate `$st` workspace and plan mutation to durable-store concurrency
acceptance: Workspace registry, plan registry, claims, sessions, migration, integration state, and workspace-plus-plan mutations use durable-store lease, fencing, CAS, and transaction APIs.
Readers reject inconsistent workspace/plan sequence or transaction marker combinations instead of accepting partial logical state.
Stale fencing tokens, stale workspace or plan sequences, transaction conflicts, and recovery-required states return exit code 2 with machine-readable diagnostics.
Locks are held only during validation, staging, publish, receipt update, and release.
`apps/st/VERSION` reflects the release-relevant command behavior change.

contract.objective: Make `durable_store` the canonical concurrency substrate while preserving existing `$st` command surfaces.
contract.background: `apps/st` already has workspace, plan, claim, session, worktree, changeset, and integration surfaces, but parts of the concurrency model live in the application instead of `durable_store`.
contract.implementation_approach: Replace local transaction, claim, and sequence-publish logic with durable-store calls, keeping receipt shapes compatible where possible and adding new fields only for concurrency/recovery evidence.
success_criteria: Workspace registry, plan registry, claims, sessions, migration, integration state, and workspace-plus-plan mutations use durable-store lease, fencing, CAS, and transaction APIs.
Readers reject inconsistent workspace/plan sequence or transaction marker combinations instead of accepting partial logical state.
Stale fencing tokens, stale workspace or plan sequences, transaction conflicts, and recovery-required states return exit code 2 with machine-readable diagnostics.
Locks are held only during validation, staging, publish, receipt update, and release.
`apps/st/VERSION` reflects the release-relevant command behavior change.
risks: Consumer migration may expose hidden assumptions in existing tests.
Version and docs must not overclaim unimplemented recovery paths.

items.step: Add concurrency, recovery, and security proof matrix
acceptance: Tests cover the 30 numbered scenarios from the spec, including malformed lock/transaction fuzz cases.
Concurrent writer tests prove one writer wins and stale writers fail semantically.
Opposite lock-order requests cannot deadlock because canonical ordering is enforced.
Security tests cover symlink attack, traversal, bounds, and final-destination verification.
Error mapping tests prove `$st` returns exit code 2 for concurrency and recovery states.

contract.objective: Close the spec's proof matrix and prove compatibility with the full repository test gate.
contract.background: The feature is only useful if hostile paths, crashes, and concurrent writers are covered by tests rather than only happy-path receipts.
contract.implementation_approach: Add focused tests near `durable_store` for substrate behavior and `apps/st` tests for command-level exit codes and workspace/plan atomicity.
success_criteria: Tests cover the 30 numbered scenarios from the spec, including malformed lock/transaction fuzz cases.
Concurrent writer tests prove one writer wins and stale writers fail semantically.

The st CLI must expose a `.ledger/st` workspace root with workspace initialization and machine-readable status as the canonical multi-plan storage entrypoint.
The st capability surface must advertise workspace-v1 storage features separately from the legacy single-plan feature set.
Workspace initialization must create only `.ledger/st` artifacts for the new canonical root and must reject accidental overwrite.
The `.ledger/st` workspace must own a plan registry so multiple independent plan graphs can be registered under one repository workspace.
Plan-local graph files must live under `.ledger/st/plans/PLAN_ID/plan.jsonl` and be created only through workspace plan commands.
Duplicate plan IDs must be rejected while distinct plan IDs may be listed and shown from the workspace registry.
Existing plan-local graph commands must accept workspace and plan scope so one registered plan can preserve current graph-mode behavior under `.ledger/st/plans/PLAN_ID/plan.jsonl`.
Plan selection must fail closed when a referenced plan is missing or inactive, while preserving one-plan operation through explicit workspace registry scope.
The same local task ID must be valid in different registered plans without cross-plan mutation.
Workspace and plan scope must accept environment defaults `ST_WORKSPACE` and `ST_PLAN`, with CLI arguments taking precedence.
Plan-local commands in workspace mode must infer scope only when exactly one active plan is registered.
Missing plan scope with two or more active plans must fail closed instead of mutating an arbitrary plan.
The workspace plan registry must support pause, resume, complete, and archive lifecycle transitions.
Plan selection and one-plan inference must count only active registered plans.
Pause/resume/complete/archive lifecycle behavior must be covered by focused tests.
Qualified references using the `plan://PLAN_ID/LOCAL_ID` shape must parse and validate through a shared command surface.
Cross-plan dependency edges must be workspace-owned and mutated only through workspace plan commands.
Valid cross-plan edges, unknown plans, unknown items, nonblocking links, and edge mutation through workspace commands must be tested.
Mutating workspace commands must use durable-store prepare, compare-and-swap publish, commit records, and recovery instead of direct append/write paths.
Workspace resources must parse, normalize, reject unsafe paths, and compute conservative conflicts across path, symbol, generated, schema, service, Git, and repo-global scopes.
Claims, leases, fencing tokens, heartbeats, reclaim, release, conflicts, and amendments must be workspace-global and fail closed on stale authority.
Sessions and projections must be session-scoped views bound to plan, claim, fencing token, workspace sequence, plan sequence, branch epoch, and projection digest.
Workspace aperture and cross-plan readiness must select deterministic conflict-free candidates across active plans and block hard cross-plan dependencies.
GCR-v2 must prove current workspace, plan, branch, claim, fencing, resource, session-view, debt, and waiver authority before execution is allowed.
External worktrees and change sets must bind worker output to a valid claim, derive changed paths from Git, and reject files outside resource authority.
Target-branch integration must serialize queued change sets, verify target head and branch epoch, apply with alternate index or clean worktree, and emit complete receipts.
Proof receipts must bind workspace, plan, branch epoch, tree digest, and dependency cuts, and integrations must stale only affected proof without deleting history.
Migration from `.step/st-plan.jsonl` to `.ledger/st` must be atomic, parity-audited, idempotent, and leave the legacy root read-only in workspace mode.
Capability, audit, doctor, import/export, docs, release metadata, and end-to-end receipts must expose the implemented STW-v1 surface for `$seq`.
`libs/durable_store` must provide short-lived lease locks with DLK-v1 owner metadata, timeouts, refresh/release/reclaim, and machine-readable receipts.
Fencing tokens must be allocated by authority-scoped monotonic counters, never caller-chosen or reused, and fail closed on overflow or counter corruption.
Text writes must support digest, sequence, and existence compare-and-swap with semantic concurrency receipts and mismatch errors.
Durable transactions must use DTX-v1 prepare, staged writes, deterministic publish, commit markers, bounded receipts, and deterministic recovery.
Multi-lock APIs must canonicalize resources in workspace, plan, branch/integration, then lexical order and reject duplicate aliases.
Path handling must reject traversal, symlink components, unsafe lock or transaction directories, hard-link substitution where detectable, oversized files, and excessive directory counts.
JSONL state APIs must read snapshots and commit snapshots through validation plus CAS instead of read-append-rewrite mutation.
Existing durable-store behavior and legacy APIs must remain compatible while being documented as unsuitable for coordinated multi-record mutation.
`apps/st` workspace and plan mutations must use durable-store fencing, CAS, and transactions so workspace plus one or more plan files mutate atomically.

The implementation must prove lock metadata, retry, stale-token rejection, reclaim, token monotonicity, CAS pass/fail, transactions, recovery, lock ordering, path security, legacy regression, JSONL validation, fsync/rename failures, receipt canonicalization, and malformed record fuzz cases.
Concurrency and recovery failures must map to `$st` exit code 2 and machine-readable lock or transaction state.
Release-relevant CLI changes must update `apps/st/VERSION`, local proof, PR proof, guarded landing, and cleanup evidence.
